newsitem.title: UK: UK biotech set for "dramatic growth" - consultant.
newsitem.headline: UK biotech set for "dramatic growth" - consultant.

text.p: The UK's biotech sector is set for "dramatic growth" over the next two years, business advisor Arthur Andersen said on Thursday.

In a report on the sector, Arthur Andersen said the number of biotechnology companies in the Britain had risen by 32 percent in the past three years to 221, with the number of biopharmaceutical companies doubling to 78.
It said the UK already had seven of the world's 20 highest capitalised biotech drug companies.

"Revenues have risen by 50 percent to 702 million stg, supported by major product development progress over the last three years, with research and development expenditure rising by 46 percent to 190 million pounds," it said.
Biotech companies have raised 1.1 billion stg since June 1995 to finance this growth.
"We expect the industry to raise an additional 1 billion stg over the next two years to further develop existing products and finance acquisitions," the report said.

It forecast a rise in the number of biotech companies to 300 by the end of 1998, with the number of drug companies doubling again to 154. "This level of growth will make the UK biotech sector one of Britain's fastest-growing industries," Arthur Andersen said.

It predicted that revenues could double to around 1.5 billion stg in the next two years "if companies achieve their projected growth targets," with research and development costs rising 70 percent to 319 million stg.

Stuart Henderson, who heads Arthur Andersen's UK Biotechnology group, said "this increase reflects the rise in the number of innovative therapeutic products reaching the later stages of expensive clinical trials and increased research on new diagnostic, environmental and agricultural products for new markets and applications."
Henderson predicted a rise in employment by biotech companies of 30 percent by the end of 1998 to 13,780 from 10,590.
